summary.intent: Audit stale/pending todos for drift across Phases 70/70.1/71, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness), handling any CI issues that surfaced along the way.
summary.outcome: Phase 72 was fully planned (research+patterns+10 plans/7 waves), executed with TDD, hardened (fixed a DoS cycle-guard bug, migrated all test files off retired types, added a CI test-inclusive typecheck gate), verified, security-reviewed (fixed a HIGH-severity moveItem write-chain resurrection bug plus several CodeRabbit findings), and opened as PR #602 with green CI; two unrelated CI regressions (#600 web-e2e, #601 desktop-e2e FUSE) from Phases 70.1/71 were also diagnosed, fixed, and merged along the way. Final merge of #602 and PR-review thread resolution were left in progress.

repo: ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) triggers only on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow definitions) to get real e2e validation before merge.

vitest does not load .env — sdk-e2e's SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported into process.env explicitly or it silently falls back to a default test secret, causing confusing 401s even when .env matches the running API.

Root `pnpm typecheck` only runs each package's `build` (tsconfig.build.json, tests excluded) — test files were never typechecked in CI, allowing ~113 TS errors (retired-type imports, vitest v2 Mock generics) to accumulate silently across 15 test files.

Playwright `ciFloor()` only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI; local runs keep short timeouts (15s/30s), so IPNS-gated mutation tests (batch delete/move, restore) reliably flake locally even when correct — must run with CI-equivalent timeouts to get representative local signal.

Setting CI=1 locally to get ciFloor's 60s timeouts also flips `webServer.reuseExistingServer` to false, causing Playwright to refuse the already-running dev API — needs a temporary config patch (revert after) rather than a real CI=1 run.

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three pieces of undone test/fixture drift: a stale desktop-e2e .mts driver using pre-rename DTO fields, an sdk-e2e assertion (Test 21) that didn't account for its own idempotency design, and it exposed a FUSE seq=1 equivocation bug.

GSD executor commits use non-conventional subjects (`feat 51-03:`, `refactor sdk:`) that fail the pr-release-preview/commitlint gate — must reword via `git filter-branch --msg-filter` before opening a PR (git rebase -i unavailable in this environment).
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body updates must go through `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
github-actions[bot] pushes a `chore(release)` commit after `gh pr create` and a passing Release Preview — always fetch+rebase before the next push to that branch.

The API doesn't log handled 4xx bodies — diagnosing a real 400 reason requires temporarily adding an axios response interceptor in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts, rebuilding, and reverting after.

code.finding: moveItem's source-folder publish never threaded baseWriteChildren into updateFolderMetadataAndPublish, unlike deleteItem/restoreFromBin — a concurrent stale republish could resurrect the moved child's WriteChildRef in the old source folder, granting write access outside the intended sharing boundary. Fixed by capturing sourceBaseWriteChildren before the drop and passing it through.

The base-aware CAS-merge only protected local's own deletes from a stale remote copy but always kept entries present in local regardless of remote — so a childId concurrently deleted by a remote writer was silently resurrected. Rewritten as a symmetric 3-way prune (base-present entries kept only if present on both sides).

collectDescendantIpnsNames had no cycle guard (unlike sibling dfsFindFolder's visited Set), allowing unbounded recursion / hang on a cyclic or malicious folder graph — a real DoS-class bug found while re-enabling a skipped test; fixed by threading a shared visited Set through all three call sites.

publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch; a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-running it collided with Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing Found results into the existing CAS-retry path instead of blindly first-publishing.

workflow: When background/verification agents flag design-level findings (e.g. 'this contradicts research doc premise'), treat them as authoritative and re-derive the correct behavior rather than accepting the plan's literal wording — one executor caught that implementing a spec's literal 'nullable returns null' would have turned a fail-closed tamper-detection throw into fail-open.

For high-blast-radius refactors (CAS-merge rewrites, bin-clearing logic), unit test passes are not sufficient proof — re-running the live sdk-e2e suite against the real IPNS round-trip is mandatory before trusting the fix.

Sequencing test-hardening/CI-gate work (fixing all test-file TS drift + wiring CI) as the LAST plan of a phase lets it cover both pre-existing drift and every new test file the phase itself created, avoiding rework.
When a security/code-review subagent's finding overlaps a CodeRabbit finding, corroborate between the two before triaging rather than acting on either alone.
Before pushing to a shared branch, always re-fetch and inspect any unrecognized commits (they may be the user's own work) rather than assuming they're bot noise.

friction: Extracting research/pattern-mapper/planner hook fragments from a hooks JSON file repeatedly failed because the raw JSON contained literal control characters inside string values — required writing a custom lenient parser script (.cjs) to work around it.

Local full-workflow.spec.ts verification runs cascaded through a chain of unrelated flakes (4.10 batch delete, 4.11 batch move, 2.1 create-folder) before ever reaching the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2), consuming ~6 sequential ~10-20min local runs.
Checked the wrong todo directory initially (resolved/ instead of completed/), requiring a user correction mid-turn.
git commit hung for ~2 minutes due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt (known recurring issue) even though the commit had actually landed, requiring separate verification.
`gh workflow run -f ref=` returned HTTP 422 because main's workflow definition predated the ref input; had to discover `--ref <branch>` as the working alternative.

A stale built API process on :3000 caused persistent 401 'Invalid test login secret' errors that looked like code failures but were actually a stale dist not reflecting current .env — needed explicit process kill + restart from source.
CI=1 locally broke webServer reuse against the already-running dev stack, forcing a temporary (and carefully reverted) playwright.config.ts patch just to get CI-equivalent timeout behavior locally.
